task: predict breast-cancer-associated genes from network topology features
note: Gene-level disease-gene association, no patient decision. Undersampling = RUSBoost's internal random undersampling; DTB (bagged trees) coded forest. Fig. 2 compares DTB with vs without SMOTE (AUC). Placement of SMOTE not stated in words.

task: classify chronic kidney disease into five stages
note: Five-stage CKD; dataset [53] size and class counts not given. Ablation Table V: RF with vs without SMOTE. ROC curve only as Fig. 4 (no AUC value in text). Evaluation design beyond GridSearchCV k-fold not described.

task: classify skin lesions as melanoma vs benign from multispectral bands
note: LOO over 32 lesions (7 melanoma); SMOTE run five times with qualified majority vote. Placement of SMOTE relative to each LOO fold not explicit; whole-data balancing stated for SVM grid search. Modality: 55-band mean-ROI spectral vectors.

task: predict credit card customer churn at a bank
note: Bank credit-card churn coded business (churn) rather than finance. Compares five classifiers with and without k-means customer segmentation; no model trained without SMOTE.

task: predict above-average postoperative length of stay after isolated CABG
note: No SMOTE: random over/undersampling, 'Both' (over plus under) and ROSE (smoothed bootstrap, coded other); 20 models compare resamplers. Authors flag oversampling-before-split overfitting in Discussion. Original 216 AA vs 405 AB.

task: detect radical content in Indonesian tweets
note: Oversampler unnamed (coded other). Order of resampling and split not described. Table 5 arithmetic: undersampling-arm test positive share >=0.37 vs <=0.32 for oversampling, so test sets differ; undersampling may have preceded the split.

task: identify opinion leaders in a cyclist community from questionnaire responses
note: 120 cyclists; training labels from top-x% self-assessment scores, test labels from peer votes (same members apparently). SMOTE then Spread Subsampling in Weka. HDDT compared (skew-insensitive tree, not coded as weights). Table 3 accuracy figures internally inconsistent.

task: predict depression (PHQ-9 >= 10) in adults aged 65 and over
note: Temporal external validation (train 2005-2020, test 2021-2023 NHANES). SMOTE plus random undersampling; no model without resampling. Text says F1 reported but Table 2 gives sensitivity, AUC, accuracy, specificity only.

task: detect Asian giant hornets in public sighting photos
note: Flipping (x4) of all 19 positives before the split, so flipped copies of one image can sit in train and test; Sec. 4.2 applies Borderline-SMOTE to the 48 training positives only (697 synthetic). Flipping coded other.

task: predict anaemia in children aged 6-59 months from survey data
note: Text claims SMOTE (themis) on training data only and an untouched 20% test set, but Table 1 metrics come from 5-fold CV on the over-sampled training set (Sec. 2.4.2); F1 .755 also fits 50% positives.
